source_refs.note: Topic 9.12 (PDF 210, printed 207). The definition's 'no charge' (no change) is marked with a Book correction box.

blocks.text: When a potential difference V is applied across the ends of a conductor, a current I starts flowing through it. The Ohm's law states that:

blocks.title: Ohm's law
blocks.text: The current flowing through a conductor is directly proportional to the potential difference applied across the conductor, provided there is no charge in the physical state of the conductor.

blocks.title: Book correction
blocks.text: “no charge” is a misprint for “no change”: the law holds as long as the physical state of the conductor (for example its temperature) does not change.
where R is a constant known as resistance of the conductor. The SI unit of resistance is ohm denoted by the Greek capital letter omega (Ω), and is defined as:

blocks.title: Ohm
blocks.text: The resistance of a conductor is 1 ohm if a current of 1 ampere flows through it when a potential difference of 1 volt is applied across its ends.
